newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook - China key as recovery seen.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook - China key as recovery seen.

text.p: Asian oil products are expected to recover some of their recent big losses as China slowly returns to the market while cuts to refinery runs keep supplies in check, traders said on Tuesday.
Gas oil and fuel oil are poised to lead the gainers as both products came under tremendous downward pressure in recent weeks in the absence of buying interest from China.
Traders said China had just prior to the Lunar New Year holidays, which began on February 7, started to buy end February arrival gas oil cargoes.
One major reported selling a 30,000-tonne cargo late last week at $1.20 per barrel premium to spot Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis.
Others reported China buying from South Korea for end February and March arrival cargoes with more purchases anticipated towards the end of this week.

Gas oil prices, which peaked at a traded $34.45 per barrel free-on-board Singapore in early December, traded below the $25.00 mark last week. But most traders expected prices to hover above this due to the new demand.
Jet fuel is expected to extend its recent rally on tight supplies with most refiners in Singapore sold out for February lifting cargoes.

Strong demand from Indonensia and rare arbitrage exports from South Korea to the U.S. have kept the market firm and prices are expected to stay above the $31.00 per barrel level in Singapore, traders said.

The high sulphur fuel oil market was also on course for a recovery as the previously rejected cargoes from China have been absorbed into the market and Mideast cargoes heading east by February have mostly been sold, traders said.
Traders said while at least two cargoes from South Korea, for end February lifting, remained unsold and additional supplies from Kuwait were still seeking homes, buyers have started to emerge.

The market would be looking out for Taiwan's tender to buy one more March cargo of low sulphur fuel oil after having purchased two cargoes in an earlier tender. The latest tender, to buy the 38,000 tonne cargo for March 11-30 delivery, closes on Wednesday.
One trader said China's demand for fuel oil is expected to pick up, with some traders returning to the office after an absence of nearly a week.

On the other hand, gasoline prices, which have firmed in recent weeks, slipped slightly as supplies improved with a Dutch trader emerging to offer high octane cargoes lifting end February to early March while a European major offered the low 92-octane.

But in the pre-holiday lull, the two players dominated the market by taking opposite stances with the bid, often higher than the offer, but for different timings. On Thursday, a US major bought the 95-octane cargo at $27.10 per barrel.

Traders said supplies in March were healthier but most were holding on to cargoes ahead of India's buying tender for four 25,000-tonne 87-octane leaded cargoes for delivery all in the first half of March. The tender closes on February 12 and valid for February 14.

The market also looked towards Taiwan to announce another tender for March 95-octane unleaded reformate cargoes after the holidays. It had only purchased one 250,000-barrel cargo due to record high offers and award at $27.60 per barrel c-and-f Taiwan but required more cargoes.
